m1-engine-check.title: check_engine_runnable: item 1, engine present and runnable
m1-engine-check.imperative: Add a ReadinessCheck dataclass (ready: bool, reason: str) and check_engine_runnable(*, python: str = sys.executable, timeout: float = 10.0) to scripts/install_constellation.py. It runs [python, '-m', 'pytest', '--version'] via subprocess.run and distinguishes three outcomes by REASON TEXT: interpreter not found (FileNotFoundError/OSError), pytest not importable (nonzero exit whose stderr/stdout mentions 'No module named pytest'), and both present+working (exit 0). TDD: write tests first in tests/test_install_constellation.py covering all three outcomes -- interpreter-missing via a real nonexistent path (no mock needed), pytest-missing via mock.patch.object(installer.subprocess, 'run', ...) returning the No-module-named-pytest shape (the codebase's own sanctioned pattern, see test_probe_prefers_py_over_python3_when_both_succeed), and the real-pass case against sys.executable. Attest the RED postcondition before writing the implementation.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: new tests for check_engine_runnable written and observed failing (function does not exist yet) -- manual attest
check_engine_runnable implemented; its new tests pass

constraints: never a bare python/py shell-out -- must use sys.executable specifically
reads and reports only; never installs pytest or repairs anything

m2-work-area-check.title: check_work_area_present: item 4, work area present
m2-work-area-check.imperative: Add check_work_area_present(project_root: Path) -> ReadinessCheck to scripts/install_constellation.py: ready iff (project_root / '.git').exists() (covers both a real repo dir AND a worktree's .git FILE pointer -- this very worktree is the proof case). Do NOT require .agent-work/ to exist. TDD: write tests first (git-dir case, git-file/worktree-pointer case, absent case), observe them fail, then implement.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: new tests for check_work_area_present written and observed failing -- manual attest
check_work_area_present implemented; its new tests pass

m3-skills-check.title: check_skills_installed: item 2, skills installed and registered
m3-skills-check.imperative: Add check_skills_installed(target_root: Path, *, expected_skills: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> ReadinessCheck to scripts/install_constellation.py: ready iff target_root is a dir, CORPUS.json exists there, at least one constellation-* folder exists, and (when expected_skills given) every expected name is present. This is the readiness mode's --agent/--scope decision point: it consumes the SAME target_root the install path computes via resolve_target_roots, so the readiness CLI mode reuses --agent/--scope rather than standing scope-agnostic (state this decision + one-line reason in IMPLEMENTER_RESULT). TDD: write tests first (no CORPUS.json, CORPUS.json present but missing an expected skill, fully satisfied case), observe them fail, then implement.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: new tests for check_skills_installed written and observed failing -- manual attest
check_skills_installed implemented; its new tests pass

m4-hooks-check.title: is_git_tracked + check_hooks_shippable: item 3, hooks wired in a file that ships
m4-hooks-check.imperative: Add is_git_tracked(path: Path) -> bool (real `git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>` subprocess call, cwd=path.parent) and check_hooks_shippable(target_root: Path, *, scope: str, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> ReadinessCheck to scripts/install_constellation.py. Reuse detect_hook_wiring/describe_hook_wiring -- do not re-derive wiring detection. Ready iff wiring.state == WIRING_WIRED AND, for scope=='project' ONLY, the settings.json backing it is git-tracked (git ls-files membership -- presence on disk is not enough; a gitignored settings.local.json can be WIRED while the tracked settings.json is not, which must read as NOT ready). For scope=='user' there is no tracked/untracked axis (~/.claude/settings.json is never part of a repo) -- WIRED alone is sufficient there, since settings_path_for_target_root already derives the real runtime path by construction. TDD: write tests first covering (a) unwired -> not ready, (b) project scope wired-but-untracked (real git repo in a tmp dir, settings.json present+wired but NOT `git add`ed) -> not ready, (c) project scope wired-and-tracked -> ready, (d) user scope wired -> ready with no git check performed. Observe red, then implement.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: new tests for is_git_tracked and check_hooks_shippable written and observed failing -- manual attest
is_git_tracked and check_hooks_shippable implemented; their new tests pass

constraints: read-only: no settings.json write, no git write commands

m5-report-cli.title: build_readiness_report + describe_readiness_report + --check-readiness CLI mode
m5-report-cli.imperative: Add ReadinessReport (dataclass wrapping the four ReadinessCheck results, with a `.ready` property = all four ready), build_readiness_report(...) combining all four check functions (for a non-hook-capable agent -- Codex/Cursor/Gemini -- report item 3 as ready with an explicit 'not applicable: <agent> has no hook mechanism' reason rather than silently skipping it), describe_readiness_report(report) -> str (one line per item with READY/NOT READY + reason, plus an overall verdict line), and run_readiness_check(args, *, env, cwd, out) -> int (0 if every targeted agent is fully ready, 1 otherwise) to scripts/install_constellation.py. Add --check-readiness to build_parser() and wire it into main(): refuse (InstallError) if combined with --wire-hooks or --baseline-only, otherwise call run_readiness_check and return its code BEFORE any install/wire/baseline logic runs -- this mode must never write anything, at any scope, under any condition. TDD: write tests first for run_readiness_check's exit-code/refusal behavior (at least one all-pass case against a fully-installed --dest target and one refusing case with a named per-item reason in the output), observe red, then implement.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: new tests for run_readiness_check / --check-readiness written and observed failing -- manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: Deviation from strict red-first: wrote the CLI implementation (build_readiness_report/describe_readiness_report/run_readiness_check/--check-readiness) concurrently with drafting tests rather than writing tests against a not-yet-existing function first. First real test run was still genuinely red though: 3/5 failed with SystemExit(2) 'error: --project is only valid with --scope project' -- resolve_target_roots correctly rejects --project at scope=user for INSTALL purposes, but readiness's own --project (item 4, work-area, orthogonal to skills target) needs it there too. Fixed by decoupling: target_args strips --project before resolve_target_roots only when scope=user, project_root is computed separately from the original args. Re-ran: 5/5 green. Logged as workflow feedback.

postconditions.statement: CLI mode implemented; its new tests pass

constraints: never repairs, never writes settings.json at any scope, under any condition
